title: Choose the visual world for the SurfView demo
question: The roll assigned The Reading Room Lightbox. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Reading Room Lightbox
options.lineage: Radiology film hung on a backlit viewbox in a dim reading room
options.thesis: Every capability is hung as a film on the viewbox, its state printed in the corners like a scan's own overlay.
options.viewport: A dark reading room: the chosen chapter's brain fills one large film sheet with corner overlays (surface, layer, window/level, vertex) and L/R/S/I orientation letters at its edges; chapters hang as a slim strip of small films along the top, the lit gap between sheets is the only bright field, and the controls sit in the film's lower margin as window/level readouts.
options.risk: Dark again, like the current demo; it only escapes the dark-dashboard look if the film, corner overlays and lit gaps are committed fully.

raised.raise: One exposure scale: every element's prominence is a single film-density step, D0 to D3, mapped by one token set.
One motion clock: playback, morphs and view transitions share one timeline, with nothing animated separately.
Chinagraph yellow is reserved for marks the user makes (selection, ROI, annotations) and the active control; nothing else uses it.
One subject per sheet, surrounded by unlit film; no panel crowds the brain.
Registered pairs: where geometry changes (lateral and medial, folded and flat), both views are hung together on the box.

regions.label: film sheet: brain with corner overlays + L/R/S/I

options.label: The Figure Plate
options.thesis: Each chapter is a journal figure: lettered panels, a colour key and a caption, rendered live.
options.viewport: A white page with the chapter as figure 1: panel a (large brain), b and c (paired views or flatmap), a caption block below, and controls set as the figure's legend.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most scientific-tool demos land, and a white ground is tiring for long viewing of rendered brains.

options.label: Curved-Crease Shell
options.thesis: One crease turns a flat sheet into a rigid shell.
options.viewport: Plan and section views of a folding sheet, registered side by side.
options.case: Folding speaks to cortical inflation and flatmaps, but the cream-paper serif world is a common default and speaks to only two chapters.
options.kept: Registered paired views wherever the geometry changes.

options.label: Step Sequencer Row
options.thesis: A sixteen-step row under a running chase light.
options.viewport: A step row as the page's one unbroken line.
options.case: Fits only the time-series chapter; neuroimaging audiences don't recognise themselves in it.
options.kept: One motion clock shared by every animated element.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Rank is depth; nothing is ever boxed.
options.viewport: One still line of text over drifting star fields.
options.case: Unrelated to the audience's world and obscures controls.
options.kept: State as one consistent density scale.

options.label: Punk Paste-up Zine
options.thesis: Hierarchy is whatever got cut out biggest.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the user's own marks.

options.label: Ikebana Alcove
options.thesis: Emptiness made active around one branch.
options.viewport: One arrangement off-centre in a quiet alcove.
options.case: Too sparse for dense control panels and foreign to the audience.
options.kept: One subject per sheet, with charged empty space.

options.label: Grid Horizon Sunset
options.viewport: Extruded title over a perspective grid.
options.case: Pure costume; it says nothing about cortical data.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neuroimaging viewer dashboard (sidebar, viewer, control panel), done to full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Left chapter list, large viewer, right control panel, as niivue- and Workbench-style tools do.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other viewer demos by design.
